title: Correcting hidden sampling biases in null models of canalizing Boolean networks
summary: Boolean networks are widely used to model gene regulatory systems. Their structural and dynamical properties are commonly interpreted by comparison with ensembles of random Boolean networks generated by sampling Boolean functions for individual nodes. Canalizing and nested canalizing functions, in which one or more regulatory inputs dominate the output, capture an important feature of gene regulation.
